Which upstream failures become which tagged errors?
decisions.answer: GitConstructError <- instanceof GitConstructError; GitPluginError <- instanceof GitPluginError; GitResponseError <- instanceof GitResponseError; TaskConfigurationError <- instanceof TaskConfigurationError; GitError <- instanceof GitError; SimpleGitError
decisions.why: exported error classes, most specific first, then the catch-all SimpleGitError carrying `code` (the source sets EPIPE, ERROR)

decisions.question: Which revision of this upstream version is the facade?
decisions.why: engine 0.4.0: every Effect traced as `<Handle>.<method>` (Effect.fn: a span and a stack frame per call), a value upstream may not have as an Option, errors branded with upstream's codes as a `reason` union (Effect.catchReason) and `Failure` as the Schema of all of them, facades Equal by their upstream object, releases traced and a failed one logged, upstream's types re-exported by name and its plain values as they are, and the facade held to @effect/tsgo and the GritQL idioms; SimpleGit provided as a service (SimpleGitService); after its re-check: a facade serialises and prints as its handle's name whatever upstream's own toJSON or toString show (neither wrapped), a handle it did not acquire has no release method, a secret's value is scrubbed from failures, the release is registered before a handle is wrapped, a release that fails as its scope closes is logged, and every entry point of the built facade imports in Node; after its third fix round: upstream's failure is kept only as a `Redacted` cause, never copied, walked or printed (`Redacted.value(error.cause)` reaches it), and an error's message and declared string fields are scrubbed of each secret of four characters or more given to the call, its codes never; the error fields typed as simple-git's own objects (`config`, `task`, `git`) are carried as `Redacted`; after its sixth fix round: every failure of a stream's iteration is classified with the call's secrets (its iterator's making, each step, a step it cannot read), an acquired handle is released once by the scope (one a list holds twice, or one two calls hand back), and the facade checks that what each member gives agrees between its type and the runtime (`CheckedGives`); after its release checks: the scope releases what it acquired when it closes, whatever the user did with it (a user's own call of a release reaches upstream and changes nothing the scope does; the scope's later release that fails is logged as a warning), and an interrupted acquisition aborts upstream's call, waits for it and leaves what it gave to the scope, as Effect's `acquireRelease` does
